name: Env Var Owned-Keys Reconciliation
description: Whenever the cluster's desired env vars change (spec.config, spec.env, or a plugin/fleet controller live-patching NEO4J_PLUGINS or a fleet token onto the live StatefulSet), the cluster controller recomputes the container's env as owned-vars-applied plus foreign-vars-preserved, then re-stamps the owned-keys annotation so a later removal is detected without disturbing foreign additions.

effects.description: mergeEnvVars applies desired vars, drops names in the previously-owned annotation that are no longer desired, and preserves any foreign vars added by the Neo4jPlugin/Aura Fleet controllers.

Rewrites the owned-env-var-names annotation (and the template hash) from the desired template only — the merged env goes into a copy of it — so the next loop can distinguish a true removal from a foreign var it never owned, and never records a plugin's variables as its own (knowledge operations.md ids 134, 155).

name: Split-Brain Auto-Restart
description: When split-brain detection finds server pods whose SHOW SERVERS view disagrees with the majority cluster group (and the repair action is restart_pods), the operator automatically deletes the orphaned pods so the StatefulSet recreates them and they rejoin the majority, surfaced via SplitBrainDetected and SplitBrainRepaired/SplitBrainRepairFailed events.

effects.description: Deletes each orphaned pod identified by split-brain analysis; the StatefulSet controller recreates it so it can rejoin the majority cluster view.
Emits a SplitBrainDetected Warning event on detection, then a SplitBrainRepaired Normal event on successful repair or SplitBrainRepairFailed if a pod deletion errors.

name: Plugin Restores What Its Target Lost
description: When a Neo4jPlugin's target StatefulSet (a cluster's {name}-server, a standalone's {name}) is created or its pod template changes, the plugin controller re-checks every Ready plugin targeting it. If the template still carries what the plugin set, nothing is written and the plugin stays Ready; if something removed it (NEO4J_PLUGINS, a variable the plugin sets, a VerifiedDownload init container or volume), the plugin turns Installing, emits PluginMissing and writes it back, which restarts the servers — or, while the target is not Ready with every server available, turns Waiting and restores it once the target is. Values someone else gave the plugin's variables are left alone, and variables the cluster renders from its own spec are never overwritten. While the StatefulSet does not exist (before its creation, or for the seconds a storage expansion takes to create it again as it was) the plugin waits with no event and stays Ready; a StatefulSet created as it was is not drift (operations.md id 177).

trigger.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (the target's server StatefulSet; a standalone's StatefulSet likewise)

effects.description: Ready stays Ready when nothing is missing; otherwise Installing until the restored servers are ready, then Ready again (Waiting first while the target is not Ready with every server available).

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (neo4j container env; initContainers and volumes)
effects.description: Writes back the missing NEO4J_PLUGINS entry, plugin variable, or VerifiedDownload init container and volumes (or, on a standalone, removes a leftover env copy of the plugin's neo4j.conf settings).
Emits a PluginMissing Warning naming what the StatefulSet no longer holds.

name: Plugin Install Waits For A Fully Available Target
description: While a Neo4jPlugin's target is not Ready with every server available — a cluster with a server down (Degraded condition True inside the grace period, or phase Degraded), or still forming, rolling or upgrading; a standalone not Ready — or has not rolled out its latest spec (status.observedGeneration behind its generation, or its StatefulSet still rolling its template out), a plugin pass whose edits would change the target's StatefulSet does not write it, because the write restarts every server and a cluster short of one could lose its majority. The plugin is Waiting, looks again after RequeueAfter, and installs once the target is fully available; it is Ready only once the roll its own write caused has reached every pod. A pass with nothing to write, a settled plugin with nothing missing, and a write that repairs the plugin's own failing init container (rx-plugin-repairs-own-init-container) are not held.

effects.description: Waiting ("Waiting until … is Ready with every server available …") instead of Installing; Installing again once the target is.
Emits one PluginInstallDeferred Normal event when the wait starts (or one PluginMissing Warning that says it waits, for a Ready plugin whose target lost what it set).

name: Plugin CA Volume Follows The Target's Trusted CAs
description: When spec.trustedCASecrets of a Neo4jPlugin's target (cluster or standalone) changes, the target's own controller re-renders its JVM truststore, which changes the server pod template and re-queues every Ready plugin targeting it. A VerifiedDownload plugin then brings the shared plugin-ca volume (an optional projection of each listed Secret, mounted at /etc/plugin-ca by every VerifiedDownload init container of the target) in line with the list: added when the list stops being empty, replaced when it projects other Secrets, keys or paths, removed with the init container's mount when the list is cleared and nothing else mounts it. The plugin controller is the volume's only writer; the cluster and standalone controllers keep it as a volume they did not render. A list that is only reordered, or a volume that differs only in what the API server defaulted or in an earlier operator's required projections, is not written. The write restarts the servers, so it waits like an install until the target is Ready with every server available.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (plugin-ca volume; VerifiedDownload init containers' mount of it)
effects.description: Writes the plugin-ca volume for the new list, and the init container's mount of it when the list stops or starts being empty, in one StatefulSet update.

Installing ("Updating the plugin's trusted CAs: spec.trustedCASecrets of … changed (…)") until its own roll has reached every pod, then Ready; Waiting first ("… updating the plugin's trusted CAs restarts every server") while the target rolls its own truststore or is not Ready with every server available. The download trusts the custom CAs in addition to the init image's default ones.
No PluginMissing Warning — the user changed the list. One PluginInstallDeferred Normal event if the update has to wait for the target.

name: Plugin Repairs Its Own Failing Init Container
description: When a VerifiedDownload Neo4jPlugin's own init container keeps server pods from starting (a wrong checksum or URL, a CA the mirror needs, Init:CrashLoopBackOff) and a change to the plugin or to its target's spec.trustedCASecrets would change that init container or a volume it mounts, the plugin writes the change although the target is not Ready — but only when every server pod that is down is failing in that container, those pods are the highest ordinals at or above the partition, no pod is missing or terminating, and Neo4j's last diagnostics report no other server unavailable. The StatefulSet's rolling update then replaces the failing pods first and the rest one at a time, so no server that is up is taken down while one is short. On a standalone, whose OrderedReady StatefulSet does not replace a pod that is not Ready, the plugin deletes the stuck pod once the StatefulSet has seen the new template.

trigger.fieldName: spec.source (or the target's spec.trustedCASecrets), while a server pod fails in plugin-init-<name>

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (the plugin's init container and its volumes)
effects.description: Writes the plugin's change to a target that is not Ready; a standalone's stuck pod is deleted so it is created again from the new template.
Installing ("Writing the plugin to … although it is not Ready: its init container keeps … from starting …"), then Ready once the roll reaches every pod.
One PluginInitContainerFailing Warning, from the status write that records the repair; Waiting with PluginInstallDeferred instead when any other server is down.

name: Plugin Removes A Setting It No Longer Sets
description: When a key is removed from a Neo4jPlugin's spec.config, the plugin's next write removes the NEO4J_<setting> variable its record (StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin>) lists and it no longer sets, in the same StatefulSet update as its other edits, and records what it sets now. A variable the target renders from its own spec, one another plugin records, or one another plugin of the target sets is left alone. The write restarts every server, so it waits like an install for a target that is Ready with every server available — unless every server that is down keeps failing in its neo4j container while running a variable the removal changes (a setting Neo4j refuses at startup), those are the highest ordinals at or above the partition, no pod is missing and Neo4j reports no other server unavailable: then it is written at once and the roll replaces the failing servers first. A plugin installed by an earlier operator records what it sets at its first pass and removes nothing it cannot attribute.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template.spec.containers[neo4j].env (a standalone's StatefulSet likewise); StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin>
effects.description: Removes the variable of the removed key and rewrites the plugin's record; a standalone's pod stuck crash-looping on the old setting is deleted once its OrderedReady StatefulSet has seen the write.
Installing until the roll reaches every pod, then Ready; Waiting first while the target is not fully available for another reason.
One PluginSettingsFailing Warning when the removal is written to a target whose down servers keep failing on it; PluginInstallDeferred when it waits.

name: Deleted Plugin Takes Away What It Wrote
description: When a Neo4jPlugin is deleted, its finalizer takes off the target's StatefulSet, in one write (one rolling restart), everything the plugin wrote: the variables its record lists and those its spec sets, its tokens in the procedure lists (on a cluster each list keeps only what the other enabled plugins ask for, and gains nothing), its NEO4J_PLUGINS names — those its record lists and, in Managed mode, its own and its dependencies' — that no other Managed plugin of the target installs (fleet-management stays while the target's spec.auraFleetManagement installs it; a NEO4J_PLUGINS the target renders itself is left alone), a VerifiedDownload plugin's init container, auth volume and, once nothing mounts it, the shared CA volume, and its record. What the target renders from its own spec stays. The uninstall does not wait for a fully available target. On a standalone whose pod keeps failing on the plugin, the finalizer stays until that pod is deleted and replaced from the new template (at most five minutes from the deletion), since its OrderedReady StatefulSet does not replace a pod that is not Ready.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (neo4j container env; initContainers and volumes); StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin>
effects.description: One update removing the plugin's variables, list tokens, NEO4J_PLUGINS names, init container and volumes, and its record.
On a standalone whose pod keeps failing on the plugin, deletes that pod once the StatefulSet has seen the uninstall's template, so it starts without the plugin (operations.md id 155).

Releases the finalizer (removeFinalizer: a tested JSON-patch removal from metadata.finalizers, no resourceVersion lock; an object already gone is success, id 189) once the write succeeded; a target that is gone counts as uninstalled.

name: Disabled Plugin Leaves Its Target
description: When a Neo4jPlugin's spec.enabled turns false, the plugin controller takes it off its target with the uninstall's single write and keeps the CR: Installing while the servers restart without it, then Disabled with one PluginDisabled event. The write waits for a fully available target unless it removes what keeps the down servers failing. On a standalone the standalone controller drops the plugin's neo4j.conf settings at once (its own roll) before the plugin's write. Turning it true again installs it.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (neo4j container env; initContainers and volumes); StatefulSet annotations neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin>, neo4j.com/plugin-entries.<plugin>
effects.description: One update removing the plugin's variables, list tokens, NEO4J_PLUGINS names, init container and volumes, and its records.
Installing while the removal rolls out, then Disabled (Ready condition False, reason Disabled).

name: Refused Plugin Stays Off Its Target
description: When a Managed Neo4jPlugin's name, or a dependency's, is not one the image of its target installs — the plugin is created or edited that way, or the target's spec.image.tag moves to an image that dropped the name (5.26 to CalVer with n10s) — the plugin controller refuses it: Failed with one PluginUnknownToImage Warning, nothing written. What an earlier operator wrote of it comes off in the disabled plugin's single write, at once when every down server keeps failing on the name, otherwise once the target is Ready with every server available; the servers that crash-looped on it start again (operations.md id 170).

effects.description: Failed with the refusal (spec.name or spec.dependencies[i].name: not a plugin the neo4j:<tag> image can install; install its JAR with installMode: VerifiedDownload instead), announced once.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (neo4j container env NEO4J_PLUGINS and the plugin's variables); StatefulSet annotations neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin>, neo4j.com/plugin-entries.<plugin>
effects.description: Only when an earlier write left the plugin there: one update removing its NEO4J_PLUGINS names (recorded, or mapped when there is no record), variables, list tokens and records.

name: Plugin Hidden By The Shared Allowlist
description: When another plugin's write (or the target's own configuration) sets the server-wide dbms.security.procedures.allowlist so that it loads none of a plugin's procedures, the hidden plugin — woken by that write to the StatefulSet if it is Ready — carries the ProceduresHidden condition and emits one PluginProceduresHidden Warning; it stays Ready and the list is not widened. The condition goes when the list loads the plugin again.

trigger.fieldName: StatefulSet neo4j container env NEO4J_dbms_security_procedures_allowlist / neo4j.conf

effects.description: Set (True, NotInAllowlist) with the list and who sets it, or removed when the list loads the plugin.

name: Fleet Manager provisioning onboards the deployment
description: Setting spec.auraFleetManagement.provision on a cluster or standalone makes every reconcile pass run Phase 0 before the plugin merge and the registration: the Fleet Manager deployment is adopted by name or created, its ID recorded in an annotation, and a token minted into a Secret that Phase 2 registers once the deployment is Ready.

effects.description: Records the adopted or created deployment's ID before any token is minted, so a crash re-observes rather than registers a second deployment.
Stores the token Aura returns exactly once; status.auraFleetManagement records the deployment and token metadata.

AuraFleetDeploymentAdopted or AuraFleetDeploymentCreated, then AuraFleetTokenProvisioned. A failed Kubernetes write or an Aura refusal is a status.auraFleetManagement.message instead; a transient Aura failure is retried quietly.

name: A lost fleet token Secret is replaced or refused
description: When the provisioned token Secret is missing (deleted, or never written), the next pass probes with POST: a deployment that already holds a token is rotated only if it was never registered or the spec says tokenPolicy: Rotate; a registered token under CreateIfMissing is never rotated, since that would break a working registration.

effects.description: Cleared before a rotation, so Phase 2 registers the replacement token.
Holds the rotated token; while the Secret cannot be written, status.auraFleetManagement.message says the token was rotated and why it could not be kept.
One AuraFleetTokenRotated Warning once the new token is stored; a refused rotation is a status message, not an event.

name: Disabled Fleet Management Leaves The Servers
description: When a cluster's or standalone's spec.auraFleetManagement is turned off (enabled false, or the block removed), the operator takes out what it added for it, in one roll: Fleet Management's procedure lines leave neo4j.conf, and the fleet-management entry it recorded leaves NEO4J_PLUGINS in the StatefulSet write that rolls the servers for that conf change. A Neo4jPlugin's entry and the deployment's own spec.env list stay. Turning it on again adds and records the entry again (operations.md id 222).

effects.description: fleetManagement.* leaves dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted and the allowlist line; on a standalone the allowlist * set against the image's default goes too.

effects.fieldName: StatefulSet.spec.template (neo4j container NEO4J_PLUGINS); StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/aura-fleet-management-entries
effects.description: One update — the conf change's restart stamp on a cluster, the write carrying the new conf hash on a standalone — removes the recorded fleet-management entry and the record; a removal no conf change carries is written alone.
